threads.body: [Concurrency] `withDeliveryAccounting` only snapshots the current unrecorded count; the delivery is not marked until `onEnd`. If two processing attempts overlap on the same retained message, both can capture `1` and each emit `messaging.client.consumed.messages`. This is reachable with asynchronous completion because callbacks attached after the instrumentation callback may run first and synchronously start another attempt. Atomically claim each delivery at operation start, store the claimed count in the context, and record only that claim at end.

threads.body: [General] `Spliterators.spliterator(iterator(), ...)` does not match `TracingIterator`'s lifecycle. The iterator starts a process span in `next()` and closes it only on a later `hasNext()`/`next()` call, so a short-circuiting stream such as `findFirst()` leaves the selected span and scope open. Parallel traversal is also unsafe because splitting drains iterator elements before the stream actions run, ending their spans too early and potentially leaving the last scope open. Use a dedicated spliterator that brackets each action with span start/end and has defined split behavior, and reuse it for `TracingListView`.

threads.body: The new sublist view preserves tracing through `iterator()`, but inherited `listIterator()` and `listIterator(int)` use `AbstractList`'s index-based implementation and never reach this override. Traversing a sublist with either API therefore skips the SDK process span and stable consumed-message accounting. Override both list-iterator paths with a tracing `ListIterator` wrapper so the new view preserves the fallback consistently.

Wait until the mode-specific delete span has been exported before branching or returning.

threads.body: [General] A `Consumer` can still propagate a checked throwable via sneaky-throw (for example, Lombok `@SneakyThrows`). This multi-catch lets that failure escape while `error` remains null, so the processing span and duration are ended as successful. Catch and rethrow `Throwable` so every callback failure is attributed.

threads.body: [Performance] This wrapper strips the `RandomAccess` marker that `ArrayList.subList()` normally preserves, even though indexed access remains constant-time. JDK collection algorithms use that marker to choose indexed implementations, so instrumented SQS response sublists can take slower iterator paths solely because instrumentation is active. Preserve `RandomAccess` on the view.

threads.body: [General] This view inherits `AbstractCollection.contains()` and `AbstractList.indexOf()`/`lastIndexOf()`, which short-circuit immediately after `iterator().next()` finds a match. Because this class routes those methods through the tracing iterator, the selected message's scope is never closed and its process span never ends, leaving that consumer context current after the list method returns. Override the short-circuiting collection methods to delegate directly (or otherwise bracket their traversal) instead of letting them use the lifecycle-based iterator.

threads.body: [General] `TracingListView` inherits `AbstractList.equals`, which traverses via this overridden `listIterator()`. On the first unequal element, `equals` returns immediately after `next()` started a processing span, without another `hasNext()`/`next()` call to close it; this leaks the processing scope and leaves the span open merely from comparing a sublist. Override equality to compare through a non-tracing delegate (and similarly avoid tracing for `hashCode`) rather than routing lookup operations through the lifecycle iterator.

threads.body: [General] This only bypasses tracing when the other operand is another `TracingListView`. Comparing a view with its owning `TracingList` in either direction still makes the JDK equality implementation iterate the traced operand. An equal comparison consumes the one allowed traced traversal, while an unequal comparison can return immediately after `next()` and leave the process scope open. Handle root/view equality through non-tracing element access so collection comparison cannot become the processing boundary.

threads.body: [General] On Java 8, `ArrayList` inherits `equals` and `hashCode` from `AbstractList`, and those implementations call the virtual `listIterator()`. This fallback therefore still turns `tracingList.equals(anOrdinaryList)` into the one traced traversal (and may leave a scope open on the first mismatch); the inherited root `hashCode()` does the same. Compare all `List` operands by indexed access and override `hashCode()` similarly so these object methods cannot consume processing ownership.
